Lina: Uploading new weights + tokenizer for open-k-lite v1.2. I put the tarball in the staging S3 bucket — need registry entry, provenance info, and a plan for quantization experiments. Who can own the intake?

Omar: I can take intake. Quick checklist idea: (1) verify checksums, (2) sign artifact, (3) add registry record with metadata, (4) run small eval harness, (5) schedule int8/4bit runs.

Priya: Please include tokenizer provenance too — tokenizer.json and vocab sha. Last time we missed a tokenizer mismatch and saw subtle tokenization drift.

Lina: Yup — I uploaded these: 
```
S3: s3://redwood-models/staging/open-k-lite/v1.2/open-k-lite-v1.2.tar.gz
sha256: 3b7f9c2a8a1d4e2f8c9a1b0e4a6f9d6c2a3e4b5c6d7e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7
tokenizer: s3://redwood-models/staging/open-k-lite/v1.2/tokenizer.json
vocab_sha256: d4c3b2a19f0e8d7c6b5a4f3e2d1c0b9a8f7e6d5c4b3a29108f7e6d5c4b3a2f1
metadata: {model_family: "open-k-lite", arch: "decoder-only", params: "6B", hf_repo: "hf/open-k-lite", sample_seq_len: 1024}
```

Sam: Nice. Two quick asks: 1) add a small reproducible ingest command we can run in CI, and 2) include an eval prompt set name so we pin the regression checks.

Omar: Proposed ingest snippet (CI-friendly):
```
# download and verify
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/staging/open-k-lite/v1.2/open-k-lite-v1.2.tar.gz ./
sha256sum open-k-lite-v1.2.tar.gz | grep 3b7f9c2a8a1d4e2f8c9a1b0e4a6f9d6c2a3e4b5c6d7e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7
# unpack and sign (if needed)
mkdir -p /tmp/model && tar -xzvf open-k-lite-v1.2.tar.gz -C /tmp/model
cosign sign --key ksm://projects/redwood/signer open-k-lite-v1.2.tar.gz
# registry put (internal CLI)
redwood-registry put --path /models/open-k-lite/v1.2 --s3 s3://redwood-models/staging/open-k-lite/v1.2 --sha256 3b7f9c2a... --tokenizer-sha d4c3b2a1... --metadata "arch=decoder-only,params=6B"
```

Priya: For the eval set let's use `prod-check-100` and `safety-smoke-10` as the quick CI suites. If both pass, we can queue the quantization runs. Pass/fail thresholds: PPL change <= +0.5, Rouge/F1 delta <= 0.02, and no >5% hallucination increase on the chat prompts.

Lina: Good. For quantization experiments I propose two tracks: A) fast int8 linear-only (no KV-cache changes) for latency/cost numbers, B) full 4-bit with llama-adaptive kernels for lowest-cost runs. Both should record latency tail p95 and sample generation quality.

Sam: I'll schedule Track A on a single GPU node (testpool-gnode-3) and log perf with the usual harness. Omar — can you create the registry entry and attach the cosign signature URL and an attest file (sigstore) to the record?

Omar: On it. Creating record now. Registry record fields I'm adding: name, version, s3_path, sha256, tokenizer_sha, cosign_url, attestation_url, uploader, provenance_notes, eval_suites (prod-check-100,safety-smoke-10), quantization_tracks (int8,4bit).

eng-ci-bot: artifact-scan: completed for open-k-lite v1.2 — vuln: none detected — scanner-report: https://ci.internal/reports/scan/1770004321 

Priya: Small nit: add `original_hf_commit` field pointing to the model on HF so we can trace back weights->source. Also store the tokenizer version from tokenizers lib (e.g., tokenizers==0.13.2).

Omar: Added those. Record now: https://registry.internal/models/open-k-lite/v1.2 — please review and mark `ingest:approved` if everything looks good.

Lina: Reviewing now. Quick QA: run `small_infer.py` with a representative prompt and compare tokens/outputs to HF reference to ensure no drift after packaging. If results mismatch, do not promote.

Sam: Test run done (Track A baseline): p95 latency 180ms, p50 40ms, token throughput 1300 tps, eval prod-check-100 passed (PPL +0.12). Uploading logs to the registry entry.

Priya: Thanks. Action items: Omar — finalize registry record + attach cosign + attestation. Sam — run int8 CI and post perf+quality. Lina — run HF parity check and sign off tokenizer. I'll monitor eval dashboards and flag regressions.

Omar: Done. Marking `ingest:approved`. Link: https://registry.internal/models/open-k-lite/v1.2/records/acceptance-1770004321

Lina: Approved. Moving to canary rollout for Dedicated pools tomorrow morning. :rocket:
